extracted.intended_audience: physicians, AMA members, healthcare policymakers, and legal advocates interested in Medicare rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes an AMA Litigation Center friend-of-the-court brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to require HHS/CMS to follow the Medicare statute's notice-and-comment rulemaking procedures, particularly when CMS changes payment methodologies. Focus is on the legal and policy rationale for requiring public comment in Medicare rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare statute requires notice-and-comment rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief calls on the court to require that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), which oversees CMS, follow the Medicare statute that requires notice-and-comment rulemaking even if it seems burdensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page argues that statutory procedure must be followed rather than bypassed for convenience; compliance is a legal requirement. Failure to follow notice-and-comment is portrayed as legally improper even when agencies view the process as burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Even 'seemingly minor' modifications can have extreme consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Even 'seemingly minor' modifications in reimbursement determinations give rise to extreme financial consequences for providers and ultimately their patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because apparently small substantive changes to reimbursement methodology can impose large financial burdens, agencies should not treat such changes as trivial or exempt from notice-and-comment; impact on providers and patients is a key consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment facilitates public input, transparency, and a check on administrative power
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice-and-comment rulemaking facilitates public input into agency decision-making, as well as greater transparency and clarity on the part of the agency and in this way provides an important check against unbridled administrative power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames notice-and-comment as promoting stakeholder participation, clearer agency reasoning, and institutional checks; these policy values are presented as reasons courts should enforce procedural requirements in the Medicare context. It also emphasizes that Medicare affects millions, so 'fulsome opportunities for public input are essential.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to payment calculation methodologies for providers implicate notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The case Azar v Allina Health Services challenges whether CMS had the right to skip the notice-and-comment rulemaking process when it changed the method used to calculate payments to hospitals to cover their additional costs for serving low-income patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications to how payments are calculated (e.g., methodology for hospital reimbursements related to low-income patient costs) are presented as the kind of agency action that should trigger the notice-and-comment process; the brief asks the Court to require adherence to the statute in such cases.
